title: SpaHet: A Software/Hardware Co-design for Accelerating Heterogeneous-Sparsity based Sparse Matrix Multiplication
problem: Sparse general matrix-matrix multiplication exhibits irregular memory access patterns that limit general-purpose processor performance. Existing FPGA accelerators use fixed tiling mechanisms that efficiently handle sparsity in only one input matrix, failing to support heterogeneous input matrix sparsity.
motivation: Sparse matrix multiplication is widely used in data mining applications.
method: SpaHet uses a dual-adaptive sliding window—a technique that slides differently across each input matrix based on where its sparse data actually is—to efficiently handle cases where both matrices have different sparsity patterns. Instead of applying one fixed tiling strategy, an exploration algorithm automatically tests different ways of organizing the computation and picks the most efficient approach. A sparsity-aware merge tree then combines all partial result calculations to form the final output matrix, reusing computations wherever possible.
key_novelty: Dual-adaptive sliding window mechanism that independently adjusts to each input matrix's sparsity pattern, enabling automatic discovery of optimal tiling strategies for both matrices.
contributions: Dual-adaptive sliding window mechanism for handling heterogeneous sparsity in multiple matrices
Specialized exploration algorithm for automatic optimal tiling strategy discovery
Sparsity-aware merge tree design for maximizing output matrix reuse
7.71× speedup over CPU and 2.74× over prior FPGA sparse matrix multiplication solutions

metrics.speedup: 7.71× vs CPU, 1.1× vs GPU, 2.74× vs FPGA baselines

primary_theme: FPGA acceleration for sparse matrix multiplication with adaptive heterogeneous-sparsity handling
